## Requirement acceptance and evidence

| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Status | Evidence | Open finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `REQ-001` | The same application build accepts two different project content configurations and presents each project's own material without project-name conditionals, copied frontends or a required live parent-depot service. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-002` | The displayed project name and source references match that root. A missing or conflicting primary identity produces clear setup guidance; an optional adapter identity conflict affects that adapter without substituting another project's identity. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-003` | A reader can identify what the project does and who it is for from Home. Different projects receive substantively different explanations; undocumented purpose, scope or audience is identified as missing instead of invented. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-004` | The first-step link resolves to an appropriate documented guide, entry document or current objective. Home explains the available Work, Project knowledge, status and help destinations without advertising unavailable actions. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-005` | Each displayed document link opens the correct permitted source or clearly explains its unavailability; the page does not expose an unrestricted directory listing. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-006` | Items identify the affected record, recorded issue or next step, source and observation time. The page distinguishes no recorded items from unavailable or partial coverage and invents no urgency, deadlines, risk score or app-owned attention ledger. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-007` | Copy supplies necessary context, describes real actions, preserves source meaning and uncertainty, and avoids unsupported promotional claims. Errors explain the effect and a useful next step. Editorial review is a content inspection, not an AI-detector, voice or speech test. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-008` | Page loads do not generate prose or overwrite custom text. Supported provenance identifies the source bytes and reviewed output; changed sources mark affected copy for review. Missing copy uses a safe labeled excerpt/draft or an explicit gap. Content derived from a no-longer-permitted source is withheld. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-009` | A reader can navigate between available views, return Home, use browser Back/Forward and follow source links. Controls have meaningful labels and visible keyboard focus, information does not rely on color alone, and normal text resizing or a narrow window does not hide essential content. Missing modules have clear states instead of misleading working links. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-010` | From Home, a reader reaches terms, documented processes, relationships and supporting sources within the common app experience. Existing distinctions between asserted, inferred, derived, external and historical information remain intact. Integration does not restore ontology authoring or create a permanent second copy of knowledge semantics. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-011` | Terms and processes remain readable when graph rendering is unavailable. Relationship labels and direction are understandable; owner-supplied limits or continuation are visible. Missing process details are identified rather than invented. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-012` | Records retain their finding, applicability, evidence and recorded history or supersession. The app distinguishes remembered findings from current definitions or instructions, creates no second memory store, and explains unavailable memory access without blocking other knowledge views. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-013` | A Task view preserves its recorded objective, state, current summary, next step, blockers and completion criteria, with related documents, history and evidence where recorded. Generated indexes do not override canonical records, and unmanaged or historical documents remain accurately labeled without migration or repair. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-014` | An approved TRD is labeled as document approval, not implemented work. An installed role or recorded assignment is not displayed as a running agent. Missing, failed, partial, stale and unexercised evidence retains that meaning; links between records require explicit references. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-015` | A reader can reach the supporting record and distinguish current observations from historical evidence. Unrecorded historical versions say Not recorded; a current digest is not presented as old verification evidence. Copied logical references contain no credentials and are not described as permanent live-service URLs. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-016` | Known IDs, titles and supported text can be found without semantic services. Results identify their type and source. The app reports failed, unsupported or partially scanned sources separately from no matches, does not widen memory's corpus, and excludes unapproved child-project and collaboration content. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-017` | Installed, configured, disabled, incompatible, unavailable and not checked states remain distinguishable, as do static checks and runtime observations. A deliberately disabled optional feature is not presented as an emergency. Health uses existing owners and creates no new maintenance queue or repair loop. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-018` | Entries explain purpose, inputs, outputs and limits. Help covers starting/stopping the app, finding knowledge, understanding a blocked Task and resolving setup issues. A control that only copies an instruction says so; it does not claim to run a skill, start an agent or grant authority. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-019` | The core page does not require an ontology snapshot, semantic backend, graph renderer or native agent session. Failed modules show bounded, intelligible limitations without erasing other results; reads respect existing owner limits. An invalid mandatory package or unsafe root binding produces setup guidance. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-020` | These operations do not create, close, resume or repair Tasks; approve documents; publish memory/ontology; acknowledge collaboration; rebuild governed indexes; or run maintenance. Only documented app-owned transient/session state and harmless presentation preferences may change. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-021` | The browser cannot select an arbitrary root or file, gain access through project registration, execute unknown project code during discovery, or expose unsupported collaboration metadata. Each optional integration remains confined to the selected project and its owner's permitted sources. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-022` | Project content cannot execute as trusted app code, credentials do not enter ordinary copied links or diagnostics, and late or revoked responses cannot replace current permitted content. Changed routes/rendering use the same protections as the existing reader; no new broad security certification is implied. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-023` | A prepared project can use Home and available reading features without a remote service or live depot process. Launch does not run package installation/builds, download models, enable backends, apply Template updates or install a background service. Missing prerequisites produce guidance. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-024` | On the initially supported macOS host, double-clicking the prepared project's launcher needs no typed command and resolves the project relative to that launcher. Reopening does not connect to another project or stop an unrelated process. If the required runtime/package is missing, local setup guidance remains readable without that runtime. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-025` | Tab closure makes no service-stop claim. Close reading session revokes that session; Stop app affects only the owned reader and explains the effect on its other tabs. Neither stops Tasks, agents, watchers or independent backends. Shutdown uncertainty is labeled honestly, package replacement requires restart, and no short reading-session timeout is added. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-026` | New-project setup can select the same reviewed package and bind the destination's own identity/content. Template starters contain no actual depot prose, Task history, memory records, grants, credentials or runtime state; setup does not claim that static installation proves a running app. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-027` | Adoption identifies exact destinations and owned files, preserves customized prose/configuration and unrelated work, retains original setup editions, and records only the selected addition. Reruns do not overwrite later custom edits. Updates/recovery restore only operation-owned package/configuration changes, never older project history. Conflicts are reported through the existing owner. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-028` | Adding Home and the shared app does not silently retire the existing reader entry point, break supported knowledge links, or revive retired authoring credentials/routes. Any approved replacement documents its actual alternative. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-029` | One result may cover multiple requirements. Content/configuration review and the existing build/static checks are preferred where sufficient, with a concise integrated browser smoke check for the changed user flow. Add or rerun a focused test only for an identified uncovered changed behavior, observed failure or material preservation/access risk; record that specific reason. There is no one-test-per-requirement rule or inherited 50-test release matrix. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-030` | The planned and executed checks contain none of those campaigns. Ordinary readable markup, labels, keyboard use and layout remain product requirements, but no voice capability, assistive-technology certification or full WCAG conformance program is required. Unselected collaboration, management and depot modules do not gate completion. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-031` | Instructions refer to real supported commands and identify the reviewed build and selected destinations. Verification distinguishes inspection/static checks from observed browser behavior and states unexercised limits. Reusable source, Template distribution, root adoption and existing-project adoption are reported separately; no extra testing is implied merely to fill a report. | `active` | 0 | None |
